description: [VERIFY] Acne is a skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells, causing whiteheads, blackheads, or pimples.
precautions: [VERIFY] Keep face clean; Avoid touching face; Use non-comedogenic products; Stay hydrated
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] Acne is severe or widespread; Over-the-counter treatments are not working; Acne is leaving scars; Acne is causing emotional distress

description: [VERIFY] Eczema (atopic dermatitis) is a condition that causes dry, itchy and inflamed skin. It is common in children but can occur at any age.
precautions: [VERIFY] Moisturize regularly; Avoid harsh soaps; Wear soft fabrics; Identify and avoid triggers
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] Symptoms interfere with daily activities; Skin becomes infected (increased pain, swelling, pus); Treatment is not working; Symptoms are worsening

description: [VERIFY] Psoriasis is an autoimmune condition that causes skin cells to multiply rapidly, resulting in thick, scaly patches on the skin surface.
precautions: [VERIFY] Keep skin moisturized; Avoid skin injuries; Manage stress; Limit alcohol consumption
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] Patches are spreading; Joint pain develops; Over-the-counter treatments fail; Skin becomes very painful

description: [VERIFY] Melanoma is the most serious type of skin cancer. It develops in the cells (melanocytes) that produce melanin. Early detection is critical.
precautions: [VERIFY] Use sunscreen regularly; Avoid tanning beds; Check skin monthly; Wear protective clothing
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] A mole changes in size, shape, or color; A new pigmented growth appears; Any skin lesion bleeds or does not heal; Family history of melanoma

description: [VERIFY] Rosacea is a chronic skin condition that causes redness and visible blood vessels in the face. It may also produce small, red, pus-filled bumps.
precautions: [VERIFY] Avoid sun exposure; Use gentle skincare products; Identify and avoid triggers; Avoid spicy foods and alcohol
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] Facial redness is persistent; Eyes become irritated; Skin thickens (especially nose); Bumps or pimples develop on face

description: [VERIFY] Contact dermatitis is a red, itchy rash caused by direct contact with a substance or an allergic reaction to it.
precautions: [VERIFY] Identify and avoid irritants; Wear protective gloves; Use mild soap; Apply moisturizer regularly
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] Rash is so uncomfortable it disrupts sleep or daily routine; Rash is sudden, painful, or widespread; Rash does not improve within weeks; Signs of infection develop

description: [VERIFY] Ringworm (tinea) is a common fungal infection that creates a ring-shaped, red, itchy rash on the skin. It is not caused by a worm.
precautions: [VERIFY] Keep skin clean and dry; Avoid sharing personal items; Wear loose-fitting clothing; Treat infected pets
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] The rash does not improve with over-the-counter antifungal treatment; Rash spreads; Rash is on the scalp; Signs of bacterial infection

description: [VERIFY] Vitiligo is a condition in which the skin loses its pigment cells (melanocytes), causing discolored patches in various areas of the body.
precautions: [VERIFY] Protect skin from sun; Use sunscreen; Avoid skin trauma; Consider cosmetic camouflage
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] Patches are spreading rapidly; Emotional distress from appearance; Want to discuss treatment options; Patches appear on large areas

description: [VERIFY] Impetigo is a common, highly contagious bacterial skin infection that mainly affects infants and young children, forming red sores and blisters.
precautions: [VERIFY] Keep sores clean; Avoid touching or scratching sores; Wash hands frequently; Avoid close contact until healed
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] Sores spread despite home treatment; Fever develops; Red or swollen area around sores; Sores do not heal within a week

description: [VERIFY] Urticaria (hives) are red, itchy welts that result from a skin reaction. They vary in size and can appear anywhere on the body.
precautions: [VERIFY] Identify and avoid triggers; Avoid tight clothing; Use cool compresses; Take antihistamines as directed
consult_doctor_if: [VERIFY] Hives persist for more than six weeks; Difficulty breathing or swallowing occurs; Dizziness or swelling of face/throat; Hives are very painful

description: Basal cell carcinoma is the most common form of skin cancer. It typically appears as a growing pearly bump or a flat red patch on sun-exposed areas and grows slowly.
precautions: Protect skin with sunscreen and wide-brim hats; Avoid tanning beds; Perform regular self-skin examinations; See a dermatologist annually.
consult_doctor_if: A persistent open sore does not heal for 4+ weeks; A shiny pearly nodule bleeds easily; A reddish patch with crusted edges appears.

description: Squamous cell carcinoma is a common form of skin cancer that develops in the squamous cells of the outer layer of the skin. It can be aggressive if left untreated.
precautions: Use high SPF sunscreen daily; Avoid peak sun hours; Wear UV-protective clothing; Regularly inspect sun-damaged skin areas.
consult_doctor_if: A firm scaly bump grows or bleeds; An ulcerated lesion fails to heal; Rapid growth occurs in a sun-damaged area.

description: Actinic keratosis is a rough, scaly patch or bump on the skin that develops from years of sun exposure. It is a pre-cancerous lesion that can transform into squamous cell carcinoma.
precautions: Wear broad-spectrum sunscreen daily; Wear protective hats outdoors; Avoid sunbeds; Monitor lesions closely for transformation.
consult_doctor_if: Patches become thickened, painful, indurated, or bleed; Lesions rapidly increase in size; Pre-cancerous transformation concerns arise.

description: A nevus (mole) is a common, benign growth on the skin that develops when pigment-producing cells (melanocytes) grow in clusters.
precautions: Monitor for changes in size, shape, or color; Apply sunscreen; Avoid picking or scratching.
consult_doctor_if: A mole changes in size, shape, or color; It becomes asymmetrical, has irregular borders, or grows larger than 6mm.

description: Pigmented benign keratosis includes benign skin growths (such as lichen planus-like keratosis) that are pigmented and may resemble other benign or malignant lesions.
precautions: Avoid scratching or rubbing the lesion; Keep skin hydrated; Protect from friction.
consult_doctor_if: Lesion grows rapidly, bleeds, changes color, or becomes painful or highly irritated.

description: Seborrheic keratosis is a very common, non-cancerous skin growth that typically appears as a waxy or stuck-on brown, black, or tan growth on the face, chest, shoulders, or back.
precautions: Avoid picking, scratching, or rubbing growths; Keep area clean; Moisturize surrounding skin; Protect from friction from clothing.
consult_doctor_if: Lesion rapidly changes color or turns pitch black; Itches severely, becomes inflamed, or bleeds.

description: Dermatofibroma is a common, benign, firm nodule that typically forms on the lower legs. It is composed of fibrous tissue and may dimple downward when pinched.
precautions: Leave lesion undisturbed; Avoid excessive shaving friction over the bump; Observe for any changes in appearance.
consult_doctor_if: Nodule enlarges rapidly, changes color, becomes persistently painful, or bleeds frequently.

description: Vascular lesions include cherry angiomas and other benign growths made up of blood vessels, appearing as small red or purple spots on the skin.
precautions: Avoid picking or scratching to prevent bleeding; Protect from trauma and sun exposure; Use gentle skin cleansing.
consult_doctor_if: Lesion bleeds profusely or frequently; Sudden rapid growth or ulceration occurs; Lesion obstructs vision or airway.
